programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing sa bhùth aig Padget ‘s e gus prèasant a cheannachd do Sula. Tha e lorg an dearbh dhèideag – slat draoidheil a tha fios aige a chòrdas rithe glan! Ge-tà, nuair a dh’fheumas e am prèasant seo thoirt seachad, tha Bing son a chumail dha fhèin! Bing is in Padget's shop looking for a present for Sula. He finds the perfect toy - a magic wand that he knows Sula will love! However, when the time comes to give to give this gift to his friend, Bing decides he'd prefer to keep it for himself!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha cearcall hùla aig Coco ‘s i fìor mhath gus cleas a dhèanamh. Ge-tà, nuair a dh’fheuchas Bing, tha e faicinn nach e rud ro fhurasta a th’ ann dhasan! Le beagan oidhirp, tha e dèanamh a chùis ach, tha e ‘n uairsin a’ briseadh a’ chearcaill...! Coco displays her talent at hula hooping, but when Bing tries to have a go, he sees that it’s not quite as easy as it looks! However, with a bit of practice, he gets the hang of it and then... breaks the hoop!

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: 'S toigh le na h-Abadas a bhith a' seinn agus a' dannsa agus tha iad cho sona ri bròg nuair a tha iad a' cluinntinn gur e facal ceòlmhor a th'ann an diugh. Cò'n Abadas a thèid a thaghadh airson am facal a lorg agus dè seòrsa turas a bhios aca? The Abadas love to sing and dance and are delighted when they hear that the day's word is a musical one. Which Abada will be chosen to look for the word and will they have a 'furtastic' adventure?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Nìp a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Tha Tilidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Mu dheireadh thall, tha Àtaidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean dha fhèin. Chan eil iad cho cumhachdach an toiseach, ach chan fhada gus am fàs iad ro chumhachdach fiù ’s! Neep and Teal find some wheels. Finally, Abney gets hold of some wheels of his own. They aren't brilliant at first, but soon they become perhaps even a bit too brilliant!

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha tòrr spòrs aig Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur an ìre gur e ròbotan a th’ annta, gus am brùth cuideigin aca putan is tha an aileag a’ tòiseachadh air Peicein. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. Why can't he stop hiccupping? Is someone else controlling him from somewhere? Greg can't stop sneezing, Laura yawns and Roman coughs. Could it be that everyone is turning into real life robots?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ leughadh Am Fuamhaire Dìomhair aig Seanair. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le David Litchfield agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Ramsay MacMahon reads Am Fuamhaire Dìomhair aig Seanair, written by David Litchfield and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Na Neachdan ann an Triantan Bhermuda, chan eil laghannan fiosaigs ag obrachadh mar bu chòir, tha iad steigte ann. Ach, le taic bho Jeffrey, tha iad a' lorg fuasgladh When the Neachdan are in the Bermuda Triangle, the laws of physics don’t seem to apply. What’s more, they’re stuck there. But with help from Jeffrey, they find a solution.

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Zach! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha e ag innse dhuinn mu Theileasgop Sheumais Webb. Bidh e cuideachd a’ beachdachadh air a’ cheist mhòr “a bheil sìon beò air planaidean eile?” Blast off into space with Astronaut Zach! In this amazing space voyage, he tells us about the James Webb Telescope and also debates the age-old question: 'Is there life on other planets?'

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Beileag ag iarraidh dealbh shnog de Phòl agus Anna, ach tha an camara a tha Deòrsa a’ cleachdadh le Granaidh, agus creid e… tha e air a ghonadh le seann mhumaidh crosta. Chan fhada gus an tig e am follais gum bi an camara seo a’ goid anam gach neach a th’ anns gach dealbh a thogas e. Betty wants a nice photo of Dave and Anna, but the camera George uses happens to belong to Gran, and funnily enough…it’s been cursed by an ancient mummy. We soon find out that this camera rather likes stealing the souls of its ‘models’.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Nam biodh dà mhiann aig Pòl, mhiannaicheadh e gum biodh fàileadh nas fheàrr à Mial-mogach agus gum biodh Granaidh na bu laghaiche. Ach ged a gheibheadh Pòl a mhiann, chan eil sin ri ràdh gum biodh cùisean na b’ fheàrr; ’s ann a tha gach miann a’ cur a h-uile sìon bun-os-cionn. Sgudal! If there were two things Dave could wish for it would be for Fuzzypeg to smell fresher, and for Gran to be nicer. But getting what you wish for doesn’t always turn out for the best, and in Dave’s case it sends nature topsy turvy. Rubbish.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi Rodgers explores the oldest topiary garden in the world at Levens Hall in Cumbria. Tha Màiri Rodgers a’ gabhail cuairt tron ghàrradh topiary as sine air an t-saoghail.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Tòmas MacAilpein is Joy’s studio guest, and Calum Maclean is on a historical trail as he introduces us to the story of the heroic Vatersay Raiders.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod gathers seaweed from the shore to put into a cake and uses locally grown vegetables in a tart.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: Ann an saoghal làn gleadhraich, ciamar a tha beathaichean a’ dèanamh ciall dheth? In a world filled with noise, how do animals make sense of it all?

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Tha soitheach a shàsaicheas agus a bhlàthaicheas ga ullachadh le Abigail – Uighean le Pesto. Cumaidh seo a’ dol thu airson ùine mhòr! A very heartwarming and satisfying eggs and pesto dish is prepared by Abigail. This will keep you going for some time! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Ann an oidhirp a bhith falainn, tha na seòid a’ coimhead ri na Meadhan-thìrean is Iapan. The lads look to the Mediterranean and Japan in their quest for healthy eating.

programme.title: So Here I Am: 100 Years of Crofting
programme.desc: Documentary from the BBC archives in which writer and historian James Hunter examines the state of crofting 100 years after the crofters of Braes in Skye fought for land rights.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Scotland's Finest: The Story of the Highland Games
programme.desc: A journey into the history, pageantry and characters that have shaped a Scottish phenomenon. Acclaimed actor Bill Paterson narrates the astonishing story of the Highland Games. From the battling clans to Queen Victoria's infatuation with her Highland subjects, the games have become a symbol of community and identity in Scotland and all across the world.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: Series re-examining the Ruth Ellis case. Gillian Pachter takes a forensic look at the police investigation and discovers worrying assumptions and problematic omissions.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: In another first-round match in the quiz competition for students, Coventry University makes its debut appearance against a team from Cardiff University, with a place in round two at stake. Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Dam Busters Declassified
programme.desc: Martin Shaw takes a fresh look at one of the most famous war stories of them all. The actor, himself a pilot, takes to the skies to retrace the route of the 1943 raid by 617 Squadron which used bouncing bombs to destroy German dams. He sheds new light on the story as he separates the fact from the myth behind this tale of courage and ingenuity. Using the 1955 movie The Dam Busters as a vehicle to deconstruct the raid, he tries to piece together a picture of perhaps the most daring attack in the history of aviation warfare. Along the way, Shaw hears from the last RAF veteran of the raid, as well as a German survivor of the tsunami which resulted from the Moehne dam's destruction.

programme.title: The Great Escaper
programme.desc: Based on the true story of Bernard Jordan, an 89-year-old veteran of the D-Day landings, who in 2014 sneaked out of his seaside care home where he lived with his wife, Rene, to board a cross-channel ferry and attend the 70th anniversary commemoration in Normandy.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie tells the story of Glenda Jackson, one of Britain’s greatest-ever acting talents and a double Oscar winner, who famously turned her back on her hugely successful screen career to pursue a life in politics. With interviews and rarely seen moments from the BBC’s archives, this programme explores Jackson’s career to gain insight into the choices and aspirations that drove her over the years. There's also a look at how those famous appearances alongside Morecambe and Wise showed that a world-renowned star, known for her serious roles and strong principles, was still capable of having fun and celebrating the ridiculous side of life.

programme.title: The Silence of the Lambs
programme.desc: FBI trainee Clarice Starling, enticing insights from confined killer Hannibal Lecter, shares her nightmare memory in the hope of stopping a serial killer before his latest victim dies. Multi-award-winning thriller.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded speaks to leading tech podcaster Scott Galloway about the growing controversy surrounding Anthropic's latest AI model, Claude Mythos. During testing, the system uncovered thousands of hidden vulnerabilities in the software underpinning most of the world's computers - prompting Anthropic to decide it was too dangerous to release. The company says Mythos can outperform humans at certain hacking and cyber security tasks, raising fresh concerns among regulators, lawmakers and financial institutions about the risks to global digital infrastructure.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team meets the couple who have been stuck in a battle with their insurer for more than three years over fixing damage to their home caused by subsidence. At the advice clinic in Reading, there is expert help for one man who suddenly discovered he had been paying a monthly book subscription that wasn’t even his for more than three years. Also on the programme, the renters stuck waiting for faster broadband because their landlords won’t approve the upgrade.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion encounters two front doors in Wigan and has a decision to make. Which one should he go through? Tommy sees a Grade II listed property in Norwich which is crying out for a sympathetic restoration. And Martin meets a London cabbie turned builder who has lofty ambitions for a flat in Kent.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In the scam hub, the team are monitoring an incredibly slick scammer posing as payment provider PayPal as he tries to defraud a woman in Essex. Nick and Harleen desperately try to call and text the woman to stop her from continuing the scam, but the scammer is so professional, he is repeatedly able to keep her onside. The only option is to get ground interceptors Harriet and Meea out on the road to try and put this scam to an end face to face.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Mammoth Graveyard
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough joins an archaeological dig uncovering Britain’s biggest mammoth discovery in almost 20 years. In 2017, in a gravel quarry near Swindon, two amateur fossil hunters found an extraordinary cache of Ice Age mammoth remains and a stone hand-axe made by a Neanderthal. Professor Ben Garrod joins the team at DigVentures during the excavation as they try to discover why the mammoths were here and how they died. Could the Neanderthals have killed these Ice Age giants?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s escapees want to raise their children near the sea, so Jules Hudson takes them to view a selection of wonderful homes in the Devon and Dorset countryside. Away from houses, Jules takes to a three-wheeled bicycle when he joins a scheme that helps people to get out and about on the area’s beautiful coastline.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of pop stars – Pussycat Doll Kimberly Wyatt, Claire Richards from Steps, Eternal’s Kéllé Bryan and Sugababe Amelle Berrabah – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of pop stars – Pussycat Doll Kimberly Wyatt, Claire Richards from Steps, Eternal’s Kéllé Bryan and Sugababe Amelle Berrabah – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

In 2017, in a gravel quarry near Swindon, two amateur fossil hunters found an extraordinary cache of Ice Age mammoth remains and a stone hand-axe made by a Neanderthal. Professor Ben Garrod joins the team at DigVentures during the excavation as they try to discover why the mammoths were here and how they died. Could the Neanderthals have killed these Ice Age giants?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s escapees want to raise their children near the sea, so Jules Hudson takes them to view a selection of wonderful homes in the Devon and Dorset countryside. Away from houses, Jules takes to a three-wheeled bicycle when he joins a scheme that helps people to get out and about on the area’s beautiful coastline.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of pop stars – Pussycat Doll Kimberly Wyatt, Claire Richards from Steps, Eternal’s Kéllé Bryan and Sugababe Amelle Berrabah – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: East Midlands Today
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the East Midlands.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: Alex Jones and Roman Kemp bring you the stories that matter from across the country.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: It’s election day, and Ian and Elaine are anxiously awaiting the results. Nicola tries to support George, and Max’s jealousy mounts.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: With the leaderboard closer than ever, all four teams leave Zaamin National Park and race towards the next checkpoint, Almaty, Kazakhstan’s former Soviet-era capital.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The week closes with the third quarter-final as the six best cooks of the week return, taking on two more challenges to prove they have the nerve and skill to go even further.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: East Midlands Today
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the East Midlands.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guests Lady Leshurr, Philippa Perry, Alan Titchmarsh and Mike Wozniak.

programme.title: Election 26
programme.desc: Laura Kuenssberg is your guide as the results of this year’s council elections in England begin to flood in. Reeta Chakrabarti crunches the numbers at her giant screen, and Professor Sir John Curtice is on hand to offer his psephological knowledge and insight. BBC regional political editors are at the most important counts, and representatives of the main political parties give their reaction to the emerging political landscape.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team meets the couple who have been stuck in a battle with their insurer for more than three years over fixing damage to their home caused by subsidence. At the advice clinic in Reading, there is expert help for one man who suddenly discovered he had been paying a monthly book subscription that wasn’t even his for more than three years. Also on the programme, the renters stuck waiting for faster broadband because their landlords won’t approve the upgrade.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion encounters two front doors in Wigan and has a decision to make. Which one should he go through? Tommy sees a Grade II listed property in Norwich which is crying out for a sympathetic restoration. And Martin meets a London cabbie turned builder who has lofty ambitions for a flat in Kent.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In the scam hub, the team are monitoring an incredibly slick scammer posing as payment provider PayPal as he tries to defraud a woman in Essex. Nick and Harleen desperately try to call and text the woman to stop her from continuing the scam, but the scammer is so professional, he is repeatedly able to keep her onside. The only option is to get ground interceptors Harriet and Meea out on the road to try and put this scam to an end face to face.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team meets the couple who have been stuck in a battle with their insurer for more than three years over fixing damage to their home caused by subsidence. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion encounters two front doors in Wigan and has a decision to make. Which one should he go through? programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In the scam hub, the team are monitoring an incredibly slick scammer posing as payment provider PayPal as he tries to defraud a woman in Essex. Nick and Harleen desperately try to call and text the woman to stop her from continuing the scam, but the scammer is so professional, he is repeatedly able to keep her onside. The only option is to get ground interceptors Harriet and Meea out on the road to try and put this scam to an end face to face.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Mammoth Graveyard
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough joins an archaeological dig uncovering Britain’s biggest mammoth discovery in almost 20 years. In 2017, in a gravel quarry near Swindon, two amateur fossil hunters found an extraordinary cache of Ice Age mammoth remains and a stone hand-axe made by a Neanderthal. Professor Ben Garrod joins the team at DigVentures during the excavation as they try to discover why the mammoths were here and how they died. Could the Neanderthals have killed these Ice Age giants?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s escapees want to raise their children near the sea, so Jules Hudson takes them to view a selection of wonderful homes in the Devon and Dorset countryside. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of pop stars – Pussycat Doll Kimberly Wyatt, Claire Richards from Steps, Eternal’s Kéllé Bryan and Sugababe Amelle Berrabah – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: Attenborough and the Mammoth Graveyard
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough joins an archaeological dig uncovering Britain’s biggest mammoth discovery in almost 20 years. In 2017, in a gravel quarry near Swindon, two amateur fossil hunters found an extraordinary cache of Ice Age mammoth remains and a stone hand-axe made by a Neanderthal. Professor Ben Garrod joins the team at DigVentures during the excavation as they try to discover why the mammoths were here and how they died. Could the Neanderthals have killed these Ice Age giants?

Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guests Lady Leshurr, Philippa Perry, Alan Titchmarsh and Mike Wozniak.

programme.title: Election 26
programme.desc: Laura Kuenssberg is your guide as the results of this year’s council elections in England begin to flood in. Reeta Chakrabarti crunches the numbers at her giant screen, and Professor Sir John Curtice is on hand to offer his psephological knowledge and insight. BBC regional political editors are at the most important counts, and representatives of the main political parties give their reaction to the emerging political landscape.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: The team meets the couple who have been stuck in a battle with their insurer for more than three years over fixing damage to their home caused by subsidence. At the advice clinic in Reading, there is expert help for one man who suddenly discovered he had been paying a monthly book subscription that wasn’t even his for more than three years. Also on the programme, the renters stuck waiting for faster broadband because their landlords won’t approve the upgrade.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion encounters two front doors in Wigan and has a decision to make. Which one should he go through? Tommy sees a Grade II listed property in Norwich which is crying out for a sympathetic restoration. And Martin meets a London cabbie turned builder who has lofty ambitions for a flat in Kent.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Hello playmates! Presenter Danny Sebastian admires a collection of items which once belonged to comedian and actor Arthur Askey. They include medals for school sports and his long service to entertainment, as well as wristwatches and theatre dressing room door plaques. It’s a double bill at Newark antiques fair as two couples try to make showstopping purchases. Each pair has £300 in their pockets and an hour on the clock. On the red team are civil servants Sarah and Graeme, and in blue are Helen and Nick. Both teams show an early interest in furniture, with the reds drawn to an imposing desk, but expert Roo Irvine isn’t convinced. Over with the blues, a recent holiday to Kenya and Tanzania inspires Helen to consider a reclining stone hippo sculpture, but Caroline Hawley won’t let them wallow in hesitation for long. In Derby, James Lewis is on the rostrum, and there are hopes and regrets over purchases. Which team will come out on top?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In the scam hub, the team are monitoring an incredibly slick scammer posing as payment provider PayPal as he tries to defraud a woman in Essex. Nick and Harleen desperately try to call and text the woman to stop her from continuing the scam, but the scammer is so professional, he is repeatedly able to keep her onside. The only option is to get ground interceptors Harriet and Meea out on the road to try and put this scam to an end face to face.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Mammoth Graveyard
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough joins an archaeological dig uncovering Britain’s biggest mammoth discovery in almost 20 years. In 2017, in a gravel quarry near Swindon, two amateur fossil hunters found an extraordinary cache of Ice Age mammoth remains and a stone hand-axe made by a Neanderthal. Professor Ben Garrod joins the team at DigVentures during the excavation as they try to discover why the mammoths were here and how they died. Could the Neanderthals have killed these Ice Age giants?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s escapees want to raise their children near the sea, so Jules Hudson takes them to view a selection of wonderful homes in the Devon and Dorset countryside. Away from houses, Jules takes to a three-wheeled bicycle when he joins a scheme that helps people to get out and about on the area’s beautiful coastline.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp hosts as a team of pop stars – Pussycat Doll Kimberly Wyatt, Claire Richards from Steps, Eternal’s Kéllé Bryan and Sugababe Amelle Berrabah – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC News at Six
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the Midlands.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: It’s election day, and Ian and Elaine are anxiously awaiting the results. Nicola tries to support George, and Max’s jealousy mounts.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: With the leaderboard closer than ever, all four teams leave Zaamin National Park and race towards the next checkpoint, Almaty, Kazakhstan’s former Soviet-era capital.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: The week closes with the third quarter-final as the six best cooks of the week return, taking on two more challenges to prove they have the nerve and skill to go even further.

Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Wild Cameramen at Work
programme.desc: Five of the best wildlife cameramen in the world have their roots in Scotland: Doug Allan, Gordon Buchanan and Doug Anderson were all born north of the border, while John Aitchison and Mark Smith have chosen to make Scotland their home. In this stunning series they revisit some of their favourite natural history moments from their global careers, and tell us how Scotland has helped them hone their specialist skills for capturing some of the greatest images to grace our television screens. Narrated by David Attenborough - the first episode of this stunning new series reveals the hardships and hazards involved when filming wildlife in the world's most extreme environments - the Arctic and Antarctic. Legendary polar cameraman and diver Doug Allan relives some of his most hair-raising encounters and returns to the place where his underwater career began - the freezing depths of a Highland river.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Planting borders and planning for cut flowers are on Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham’s to-do list at the garden. Lizzie is direct sowing in the new cuttings area and Brian is in the zig-zag border, planting varieties that will grow tall, making them ideal for the back of a plot without requiring support or staking. Brian kicks off this year’s collection of plants being cultivated in the 6x8ft glasshouse. This is the most common-sized domestic greenhouse, so if you are lucky enough to have one, Brian has some great ideas for this season. Lizzie is the first of the presenters to start work in her competition plot. The theme this year is planting that will appeal to one of the senses, and Lizzie has one of the most challenging: touch. Plus, there is a report on the alpine collection at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, and all the usual handy hints.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie, Arlene and Shahbaz head to the Isle of Bute, the jewel of the Firth of Clyde. Dougie meets island dairy farmers staying resilient as another milk pricing crisis looms. He also visits the grounds of Mount Stuart House to delve into one of Bute’s biggest wildlife mysteries. Arlene joins a 'superhero' beach ranger at Scalpsie Bay to uncover what is washing up on Bute’s shores. She also discovers how preschool children are getting their first taste of farming life. And Shahbaz meets a Syrian family who fled war and have built a new life on the island, finding welcome and opportunity there.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: On the Isle of Lewis, a police officer confronts an angry fisherman who he suspects has been illegally poaching salmon. In Fort William, police respond to reports that a young woman is attacking a man with a knife. Armed police target the operations of a violent county lines drug gang in Inverness. And in Glencoe, PC Stephen Cooper has to track down and detain a high-risk missing person.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: A portrait of Henrik Larsson, from his humble beginnings in Sweden, to Feyenoord in Holland, his seven era-defining seasons at Celtic, and Champions League glory with Barcelona.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: This episode of the spoof documentary sees Chief Commissioner Miekelson trying out some weapons, getting his portrait painted and doing 'thumbthing' about bigotry. Meanwhile, the rural police deal with a cat stranded in a boat, the urban police aren't fooled by a bluffing burglar and the traffic cops encounter a dozy pedestrian and a sleeping salesman. Volunteer Officer Ken Beattie fines a litterbug on a bridge, Operator Maggie LeBeau tells us about her heroes, and Sergeant Karen Ann Millar is offered fingerprints and some glockenspiel music from local man Bobby Muir.

programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Dynasties
programme.desc: In Senegal, west Africa, live a group of chimpanzees led by an alpha male named David. He has already been alpha for three years - a time when leaders here are usually overthrown. To make matters worse, David has no allies - no-one to help him defend his leadership. As the dry season sets in, the group are forced closer together to survive. But David is now surrounded by rivals who all want his crown and are prepared to kill him for it. David faces brutal battles, has his world engulfed in flames and has to pull off an extraordinary act of deception. In a story of power and politics, can David overcome the threats to his leadership and hold on to the alpha position long enough to sire a possible future heir to his throne?

programme.desc: A mother puma must battle rivals, tackle prey nearly three times her size and endure the wild mountain weather of Patagonia in her bid to raise four cubs – her biggest litter yet.

programme.title: Asia
programme.desc: Asia is the most mountainous continent on earth. From the forested peaks of the tropics to the hostile heights of the Himalayas, Asia's mountains are home to an astonishing abundance of specialised plants and wildlife. In India, elephants live in high-altitude tea plantations, and in Thailand, mountainous caves hide the planet's greatest gathering of swifts. In Pakistan, markhor live life truly on the edge, fighting for mates atop towering cliffs, and in Nepal, the forested foothills of the Himalayas provide hiding places for one of Asia's shyest mammals, the red panda.

programme.title: Freddie Flintoff's Field of Dreams
programme.desc: As the team struggle to get used to their new surroundings, Freddie Flintoff pushes them to embrace the local culture and cuisine. After discovering Adnan is struggling with life on tour, Freddie gets the team to rally around, which requires making some unusual sacrifices. And with the next match approaching, their first training session reveals a promising new addition to the squad, who could give the team a fighting chance of securing their first victory in India.

programme.title: The Traitors India
programme.desc: A devastating murder leaves the Innocents shocked. Players second-guess everyone's true identity, and trust becomes a thing of the past. Unaware of the Traitors' secret mission, the group ventures into a desolate no-man’s-land to build the prize pot. As tensions rise and suspicions grow, alliances are tested like never before. Consumed by paranoia, players struggle to collaborate. Can they look past their differences and focus on the real matter at hand - uncovering the Traitors? Or will the Traitors continue to rule this divided lot from the shadows?

programme.title: The Traitors India
programme.desc: The game of trust and betrayal gets tougher. This time, the players must choose between personal or collective gain. The mission forces them to second-guess even their most trusted allies and brings out their selfish agendas. As the day unfolds, the Innocents are left grappling with new theories and suspicions, and the true nature of the game continues to unravel. With every decision crucial, the stakes are higher than ever, and betrayal is always just around the corner. At the Circle, new accusations fly and old doubts resurface as the players attempt to uncover who can be trusted. Meanwhile, the Traitors face a tough choice in the secret tower.

programme.title: The Traitors India
programme.desc: Morning brings good news, but as always, happiness is short-lived in the palace. Breakfast takes a dramatic turn as four players face an unexpected twist, leaving the entire group baffled. In the mission, the players channel the mindset of the Traitors to answer challenging questions. Racing against time, the group fights to save one player from an uncertain fate, but the mission’s high stakes push alliances to the breaking point. At the Circle of Shaq, a long-doubted player gets dragged back into the spotlight. And as the night ends, the Traitors take over the secret tower to seal the fate of one of the four targeted players.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Mairéad and the lads take the family car on a road trip to pick up her unpredictable mother, but disaster strikes.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Sun and sand are the new dream, but how can the lads afford it? Enter Billy Murphy with a daring whiskey heist idea.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: It’s Humphrey’s last day as detective inspector, but there’s no time to dwell, as the whole team is eagerly awaiting the town’s annual pirate festival. Danger, however, is ahoy when Geraldine Desai’s nautical exhibition goes up in smoke, leading to the ancient treasure map of pirate Elias Cutler going missing amid the chaos. On the trail of the missing map, Humphrey soon has suspicions when he discovers that Geraldine has been selling her memorabilia to pay for her husband’s care and recently had the map revalued. Touching base with an antiques dealer, who is adamant the map is worth nothing, the team begin to question if they’re dealing with a harmless prank, an insurance job, or something more sinister. Meanwhile, Humphrey frets about a potential leaving party as Mr Smith prepares to take over. Smelling a rat, Anne recruits Martha and Kelby to launch an investigation of her own. Elsewhere, Esther braces herself to say goodbye to her daughter, unaware that Zoe has prepared a shock surprise.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc: In Eastbourne, siblings David and Theresa battle to raise money for DKMS, gambling on designer fashion, vintage finds and bold upcycled pieces.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is busy this week, as the garden bursts into colour. Woody herbs such as thyme and sage don’t thrive in his clay soil, so he’s sowing seeds to ensure a steady supply. He’s planting grasses in the new Woodland Garden, creating a colourful pot for shade and there's advice on what to do with this year’s daffodil bulbs. Carol Klein proves that small can be both beautiful and delicious, creating a modest border devoted to vegetables and weaving it together with flowers, to provide year round colour. And Advolly Richmond heads to Fife to uncover the story of the first pink cupped daffodil, bred in the early 1900s and still growing today, thanks to two passionate plantswomen. There’s a visit to a specialist nursery in Hertfordshire. With help from the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, they are preparing to exhibit trees fit for a changing climate at the RHS Chelsea Flower show. And it's all aboard a houseboat that's jam packed with plants.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores the world of content creators and how deaf people are using online platforms to share stories, build communities and challenge stereotypes. The show looks at the highs, lows and realities of social media life, from viral success and community connection to pressure and criticism. Presenter Marios Costi is joined in the studio by deaf content creator Becky Mingins, whose humorous videos about everyday deaf life have attracted hundreds of thousands of followers online. Becky reflects on how she began creating content during the Covid pandemic and how her family and personal experiences inspire much of her work.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Bristol to help a busy household of nine young professionals. Their communal areas are in desperate need of some attention: the overcrowded living room needs seating and storage solutions, the recycling area is overflowing, and the downstairs wet room proves a cleaning challenge for Maxine.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: Dominant male lions Big Toe and Madumo disappear after fighting intruders, leaving the family exposed. The team pick up sub-adult males Colin and Ngkonne. They’re coming of age but are not yet big enough to challenge intruders. Greg Hartman follows Xudum the leopard as she strays into dangerous territory looking for a mate. She must choose carefully, as male leopards will kill cubs that are not their own. And local cinematographer Rea Schulte heads to Brinke finds Pobe, the cheetah’s daughter.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Royal Holloway College in Surrey, where their discoveries include a collection of West Indian paintings worth as much as £25,000, a selection of costume designs rescued from the dustbin worth £5,000, a very short walking stick which belonged to Enrico Caruso and a pair of Delft plates which delight John Sandon.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog it comes from the Bowes Museum at Barnard castle in County Durham. The museum was purpose built to house the collection of Josephine and John Bowes.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s journey continues in Busan, South Korea’s second city, on the country’s south eastern coast. On the seafront at Haeundae Beach, he boards the Sky Capsule monorail along a former coastal railway route, reimagined as a scenic ride above the shoreline. From here, Michael heads to Jagalchi Fish Market, one of the largest in South Korea, where he explores Busan’s long fishing heritage with a local food blogger and samples the city’s famously fresh seafood. Overlooking Busan’s vast container port, Michael discovers how the city became Korea’s principal maritime gateway, handling the majority of the nation’s seaborne trade. In Jeonju, one of Korea’s oldest cities and former heart of the Joseon dynasty. Exploring its historic hanok village, he meets a master craftsman producing hanji paper using techniques refined over centuries.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Andrew and dad Terrence are spinning plates on the farm, and with their glamping pods, just as the latest member of the Glenn family arrives. Long days on the dairy shed build and an infection in Adam’s leg mean he is desperate for a new prosthetic. Meanwhile, Ally and fellow crofters set sail to the stunning volcanic Shiant Isles, where they must navigate steep cliffs to find and shear sheep.

programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programme.desc: A compilation of the most spectacular moments from the series, highlighting the rich and wonderful diversity of life found on Earth's seven unique continents. Millions of years ago, huge forces ripped apart the Earth's crust, creating seven distinct continents. Over time, each one developed its own remarkable wildlife. We see the extraordinary variety of life found in South America and visit the largest of all continents, Asia, so big it still hides rarely seen creatures. We explore the cities of Europe, full of surprises, and the wilds of Africa, home to the greatest gatherings of animals. Also, we travel to the searing heat of Australia, with its weird and wonderful wildlife, and witness the pioneering animals of North America that make the most of every opportunity. Finally, we venture to the frozen wilderness of Antarctica where, on the most hostile continent of all, life manages to thrive against the odds. And we reveal how the biggest challenge faced by wildlife today is the impact of human activity on all seven of our incredible continents.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: What really happened to the princes in the tower? Lucy Worsley uncovers the story of the two boys whose disappearance in 1483 has led to centuries of mystery and speculation.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: At the forefront of its genre, the roll call of stand-ups who have performed in front of the famous Live at the Apollo lights plays out like a who’s who of comedic royalty, and this series is no different. Each episode sees a national (and sometimes international!) stand-up both compering and performing, before introducing two of the best established and up-coming stand-ups to the stage. This episode is hosted by the inimitable Tom Allen, who introduces the fantastic Rosie Jones and the wonderful Kae Kurd to the world-famous Apollo stage. Other acts to appear throughout the series include Sindhu Vee, Alex Edelman, Lou Sanders, Darren Harriott, Jessica Fostekew, Stephen Bailey, Desiree Burch, Paul McCaffrey, Jonny Pelham, Ardal O'Hanlon, Sara Barron, Mawaan Rizwan, Guz Khan, Kiri Pritchard-McLean, Rhys James, Sara Pascoe, Chris McCausland and Flo & Joan.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: One patient’s rare penis cancer requires a partial amputation, and another patient with severe endometriosis must have a huge cyst and a damaged kidney removed.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores the world of content creators and how deaf people are using online platforms to share stories, build communities and challenge stereotypes. The show looks at the highs, lows and realities of social media life, from viral success and community connection to pressure and criticism. Presenter Marios Costi is joined in the studio by deaf content creator Becky Mingins, whose humorous videos about everyday deaf life have attracted hundreds of thousands of followers online. Becky reflects on how she began creating content during the Covid pandemic and how her family and personal experiences inspire much of her work.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: A fresh set of hopeful home cooks serve up their signature dishes and precision cooking in a bid to impress the MasterChef judges and get through to the quarter-finals.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Mairéad and the lads take the family car on a road trip to pick up her unpredictable mother, but disaster strikes.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Sun and sand are the new dream, but how can the lads afford it? Enter Billy Murphy with a daring whiskey heist idea.

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: It’s Humphrey’s last day as detective inspector, but there’s no time to dwell, as the whole team is eagerly awaiting the town’s annual pirate festival. Danger, however, is ahoy when Geraldine Desai’s nautical exhibition goes up in smoke, leading to the ancient treasure map of pirate Elias Cutler going missing amid the chaos. On the trail of the missing map, Humphrey soon has suspicions when he discovers that Geraldine has been selling her memorabilia to pay for her husband’s care and recently had the map revalued. Touching base with an antiques dealer, who is adamant the map is worth nothing, the team begin to question if they’re dealing with a harmless prank, an insurance job, or something more sinister. Meanwhile, Humphrey frets about a potential leaving party as Mr Smith prepares to take over. Smelling a rat, Anne recruits Martha and Kelby to launch an investigation of her own. Elsewhere, Esther braces herself to say goodbye to her daughter, unaware that Zoe has prepared a shock surprise.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc: In Eastbourne, siblings David and Theresa battle to raise money for DKMS, gambling on designer fashion, vintage finds and bold upcycled pieces.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is busy this week, as the garden bursts into colour. Woody herbs such as thyme and sage don’t thrive in his clay soil, so he’s sowing seeds to ensure a steady supply. He’s planting grasses in the new Woodland Garden, creating a colourful pot for shade and there's advice on what to do with this year’s daffodil bulbs. Carol Klein proves that small can be both beautiful and delicious, creating a modest border devoted to vegetables and weaving it together with flowers, to provide year round colour. And Advolly Richmond heads to Fife to uncover the story of the first pink cupped daffodil, bred in the early 1900s and still growing today, thanks to two passionate plantswomen. There’s a visit to a specialist nursery in Hertfordshire. With help from the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, they are preparing to exhibit trees fit for a changing climate at the RHS Chelsea Flower show. And it's all aboard a houseboat that's jam packed with plants.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: See Hear explores the world of content creators and how deaf people are using online platforms to share stories, build communities and challenge stereotypes. The show looks at the highs, lows and realities of social media life, from viral success and community connection to pressure and criticism. Presenter Marios Costi is joined in the studio by deaf content creator Becky Mingins, whose humorous videos about everyday deaf life have attracted hundreds of thousands of followers online. Becky reflects on how she began creating content during the Covid pandemic and how her family and personal experiences inspire much of her work.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be alright!

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit Bristol to help a busy household of nine young professionals. Their communal areas are in desperate need of some attention: the overcrowded living room needs seating and storage solutions, the recycling area is overflowing, and the downstairs wet room proves a cleaning challenge for Maxine.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: Dominant male lions Big Toe and Madumo disappear after fighting intruders, leaving the family exposed. The team pick up sub-adult males Colin and Ngkonne. They’re coming of age but are not yet big enough to challenge intruders. Greg Hartman follows Xudum the leopard as she strays into dangerous territory looking for a mate. She must choose carefully, as male leopards will kill cubs that are not their own. And local cinematographer Rea Schulte heads to Brinke finds Pobe, the cheetah’s daughter.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Royal Holloway College in Surrey, where their discoveries include a collection of West Indian paintings worth as much as £25,000, a selection of costume designs rescued from the dustbin worth £5,000, a very short walking stick which belonged to Enrico Caruso and a pair of Delft plates which delight John Sandon.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog it comes from the Bowes Museum at Barnard castle in County Durham. The museum was purpose built to house the collection of Josephine and John Bowes.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the Deputy Chief Constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s journey continues in Busan, South Korea’s second city, on the country’s south eastern coast. On the seafront at Haeundae Beach, he boards the Sky Capsule monorail along a former coastal railway route, reimagined as a scenic ride above the shoreline. From here, Michael heads to Jagalchi Fish Market, one of the largest in South Korea, where he explores Busan’s long fishing heritage with a local food blogger and samples the city’s famously fresh seafood. Overlooking Busan’s vast container port, Michael discovers how the city became Korea’s principal maritime gateway, handling the majority of the nation’s seaborne trade. In Jeonju, one of Korea’s oldest cities and former heart of the Joseon dynasty. Exploring its historic hanok village, he meets a master craftsman producing hanji paper using techniques refined over centuries.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Andrew and dad Terrence are spinning plates on the farm, and with their glamping pods, just as the latest member of the Glenn family arrives. Long days on the dairy shed build and an infection in Adam’s leg mean he is desperate for a new prosthetic. Meanwhile, Ally and fellow crofters set sail to the stunning volcanic Shiant Isles, where they must navigate steep cliffs to find and shear sheep.

programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programme.desc: A compilation of the most spectacular moments from the series, highlighting the rich and wonderful diversity of life found on Earth's seven unique continents. Millions of years ago, huge forces ripped apart the Earth's crust, creating seven distinct continents. Over time, each one developed its own remarkable wildlife. We see the extraordinary variety of life found in South America and visit the largest of all continents, Asia, so big it still hides rarely seen creatures. We explore the cities of Europe, full of surprises, and the wilds of Africa, home to the greatest gatherings of animals. Also, we travel to the searing heat of Australia, with its weird and wonderful wildlife, and witness the pioneering animals of North America that make the most of every opportunity. Finally, we venture to the frozen wilderness of Antarctica where, on the most hostile continent of all, life manages to thrive against the odds. And we reveal how the biggest challenge faced by wildlife today is the impact of human activity on all seven of our incredible continents.

programme.title: Lucy Worsley Investigates
programme.desc: What really happened to the princes in the tower? Lucy Worsley uncovers the story of the two boys whose disappearance in 1483 has led to centuries of mystery and speculation.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the Deputy Chief Constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

programme.title: The Young Offenders

programme.title: Beyond Paradise
programme.desc: It’s Humphrey’s last day as detective inspector, but there’s no time to dwell, as the whole team is eagerly awaiting the town’s annual pirate festival. Danger, however, is ahoy when Geraldine Desai’s nautical exhibition goes up in smoke, leading to the ancient treasure map of pirate Elias Cutler going missing amid the chaos. On the trail of the missing map, Humphrey soon has suspicions when he discovers that Geraldine has been selling her memorabilia to pay for her husband’s care and recently had the map revalued. Touching base with an antiques dealer, who is adamant the map is worth nothing, the team begin to question if they’re dealing with a harmless prank, an insurance job, or something more sinister. Meanwhile, Humphrey frets about a potential leaving party as Mr Smith prepares to take over. Smelling a rat, Anne recruits Martha and Kelby to launch an investigation of her own. Elsewhere, Esther braces herself to say goodbye to her daughter, unaware that Zoe has prepared a shock surprise.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc: In Eastbourne, siblings David and Theresa battle to raise money for DKMS, gambling on designer fashion, vintage finds and bold upcycled pieces.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty is busy this week, as the garden bursts into colour. Woody herbs such as thyme and sage don’t thrive in his clay soil, so he’s sowing seeds to ensure a steady supply. He’s planting grasses in the new Woodland Garden, creating a colourful pot for shade and there's advice on what to do with this year’s daffodil bulbs. Carol Klein proves that small can be both beautiful and delicious, creating a modest border devoted to vegetables and weaving it together with flowers, to provide year round colour. And Advolly Richmond heads to Fife to uncover the story of the first pink cupped daffodil, bred in the early 1900s and still growing today, thanks to two passionate plantswomen. There’s a visit to a specialist nursery in Hertfordshire. With help from the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, they are preparing to exhibit trees fit for a changing climate at the RHS Chelsea Flower show. And it's all aboard a houseboat that's jam packed with plants.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: When Danger Mouse makes short work of Burt Badboy and his newly acquired band of fanatical feline followers, the group's leader Mandy and her cult of cats immediately trade in their colourful mohican hairstyles for eyepatches and become Danger Mouse worshippers. At first Danger Mouse is having too much fun to take notice of Penfold's warnings about his new-found cult status, but even he is forced to act when the cats follow his example a little too literally and live life a little too dangerously. Danger Mouse's attempt to disown the cats goes down like a lead balloon, and they use mouse-fu skills and a superpowered amulet stolen from Tutenkamoo to show their idol the error of his ways. Danger Mouse battles the frenzied feline onslaught and saves HQ from becoming a giant scratching post. However, this only reaffirms the idea that he is the chosen one in the minds of Mandy and the cult of cats. Danger Mouse realises that the only solution is to find a new obsession for the cats.
